 Student Financial Services provides statement on federal loan cuts
 Gabriel Wheeler , Advertising Manager 
 | 
 November 2, 2026 
 USM Photo Library 
 In a recent article, The Free Press examined how President Donald Trump’s “One Big Beautiful Bill Act” changed federal student loan eligibility and has impacted programs classified as “low-earning.” To recap, the affected programs include: social work, the arts, religious studies, music, and cosmetology. This piece explores what those changes could mean for University of Southern Maine (USM) students and their ability to finance their education. 
 I spoke with USM’s Director of Financial Aid, Elizabeth Sarazin. I asked what impact these cuts would have on enrolled USM students and incoming students.  
 Sarazin said, “ The Financial Aid Office at USM has been following recent legislation about federal loan programs closely.  Upon review of early data, we are confident that the majority of our academic programs will pass the earnings test that the federal government has introduced.” 
 She continued, “This test is meant to ensure that students, on average, benefit financially from their college degrees.  The median income of our graduates is typically higher than the benchmark described in the new legislation, and we are confident that federal Pell grants are not at risk at USM. Federal guidance is still coming and we are reviewing it carefully to ensure USM is compliant with all new rules and regulations, and so that we can communicate with students if and when it becomes clear that any of our programs will be impacted. ” 
 Students are encouraged to contact the Student Financial Services by email at [email protected] or by calling 207-780-5250. It is important to note that Student Financial Services does not have additional information to provide about this issue beyond what was shared in the statements above.

 About the Contributor 
 Gabriel Wheeler , Advertising Manager 
 Gabe Wheeler is returning for his second year as the Advertising Manager at The Free Press after originally interning in the position. He is in his fourth and final year as an undergrad Business Marketing student here at the University of Southern Maine. When it comes to writing for The Free Press, he likes to write about sports and current news events. Prior to working at The Free Press, Gabe has done data-entry work, including GIS data entry for the Berwick Sewer District, prep and line cook work at Fogarty’s Restaurant, and was a Sales Associate before becoming Assistant Manager at Pepper Palace. Outside of The Free Press, Gabe likes weightlifting, watching sports, cooking, playing video games, and listening to music. With this being his final semester at both USM and The Free Press, Gabe is looking forward to building long-lasting connections while also learning from those at The Free Press and around campus!
